Pathophysiology
OA is a chronic joint disease that involves the loss of habitually 
weight-bearing articular (joint) cartilage. This cartilage nor-
mally allows bones to glide smoothly over one another. The loss 
can result in stiffness, pain, swelling, loss of motion, and changes 
in joint shape, in addition to abnormal bone growth, which can 
result in osteophytes (bone spurs) (see Figure 39-1 and Patho-
physiology and Care Management Algorithm: Osteoarthritis).
